messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] us-west2 spot-pool GPU queue spike detected. queue_length=2104, preemptions=64 in last 5m, error_rate=18%. Pager alerting @oncall-sre. https://metrics.redwood/usw2/gpu-queue
Alice (oncall): ack — joining. Creating incident channel #inc-1789456000. Bridgelink up in 60s.
Alice (oncall): bridgelink: https://meet.redwood/incident/1789456000 — joining now. Who's on infra? @Ben (infra)
Ben (infra): on it, looking at autoscaler controller logs. I'm seeing repeated errors: "ScaleUpLimitReached" then cloud API 429s. Looks like requests are being throttled by provider.
Carla (sre): visible impact: frontend router reports 22% throttles for generation requests; avg latency 2.1s (baseline 350ms). Queue backlog 2104 and growing.
Dan (ml-eng): spot flurry — many spot instances preempted simultaneously. Fallback pool binding failing: autoscaler can't attach nonspot nodes due to tag mismatch. I think recent helm rollback removed fallbackPools config.
Maya (eng-platform): checking recent deploys... confirmed: helm-release "autoscaler-usw2" had a rollback 02:12 which reverted fallbackPools to [] accidentally.
Ben (infra): trying emergency attach of dedicated pool for critical traffic:
```
./tools/attach-pool --region=us-west2 --pool=dedicated-emergency --nodes=8
```
Ben (infra): attach command failed: AWS response 403/InsufficientCapacity. Provider is returning transient capacity errors.
Carla (sre): mitigation idea: throttle low-priority customers at the router to protect control-plane and reduce queue inflow. Can we flip routing priority to prefer nonspot for new requests?
Alice (oncall): agreed. Eve, start customer impact assessment. Frank, draft initial banner. Ben/Maya, can you patch routing?
Frank (support): crafting banner now: "We're investigating degraded inference performance in us-west2 due to GPU capacity interruptions. Engineers are working on mitigation. Updates every 15m." Posting to status.redwood and affected customers list.
Eve (product): collect top affected customers and severity. I'll coordinate comms after first list.
Maya (eng-platform): applying routing patch to shift new traffic to nonspot pool:
```
PATCH /routing/policy/us-west2
{ "fallback_priority": "nonspot" }
```
Maya (eng-platform): patch applied. Observability shows ~40% of new requests routed to nonspot pool within 2m. Old queued tasks remain bound to original spot-backed assignments.
Dan (ml-eng): queued tasks require KV-cache affinity; simple reroute may drop cache locality and regress quality. We should avoid mass restart; prefer draining queue gradually.
Ben (infra): kicking off queue-drainer job to accelerate safe migrations:
```
kubectl scale job/gpu-queue-drainer -n infra --replicas=4
```
Ben (infra): drainer started; initial reduction -> queue_length=900 (monitoring).
Carla (sre): autoscaler logs show additional failures: "fallbackPoolNotFound" due to the tag mismatch Maya found. We need to patch helm chart and redeploy autoscaler with rollback-guard.
Maya (eng-platform): preparing autoscaler patch now (add explicit fallbackPools + guard). Will deploy shortly.
Ben (infra): cloud ops provisioning request for dedicated emergency capacity submitted (32 GPUs). ETA 12-18m per provider.
Alice (oncall): approve emergency spend. Prioritize critical customers. Frank, push targeted notices to top 10 affected.
Frank (support): sent targeted notices. Two customers replied with urgent escalations — CS routing to account execs.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: autoscaler patch r345 -> us-west2. Starting rollout with canary 10%.
Maya (eng-platform): canary succeeded, rolling to 50%, then 100%. Patch fixes fallbackPools tag and adds rate-limit guard.
Ben (infra): after patch, autoscaler successfully attached 12 nonspot nodes and then 8 dedicated nodes when provider capacity allowed.
Carla (sre): monitoring: queue 320 and falling; error_rate down to 3%; latency trending back to 420ms. Good signs.
Dan (ml-eng): note — some models lost KV-cache state for a subset of sessions. We'll run the lightweight cache-rehydrate job for affected models to avoid quality regressions.
Alice (oncall): runbook step executed: enable request-throttling and route-fallback, start dedicated provisioning, post customer comms. Please add notes to incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/1789456000
Eve (product): preparing public incident summary and internal RCA outline. Root cause hypothesis: helm rollback removed fallbackPools entry + sudden spot preemption spike -> autoscaler couldn't attach fallback nodes and cloud API rate limits blocked emergency provisioning.
Maya (eng-platform): confirm: the helm rollback happened as part of a separate deploy earlier today (autoscaler chart reverted). We'll pin fallbackPools in chart to avoid accidental rollback.
Ben (infra): dedicated capacity online. Monitoring queue drain and scaling metrics. Queue now 120.
Carla (sre): mitigation stable. Keeping incident state -> mitigated -> monitoring. Recommend 2hr watch and full postmortem.
Frank (support): updated customers: initial banner + targeted follow-ups sent. Collecting impact feedback for postmortem.
Alice (oncall): handing off to night oncall: Carla (sre) in 45m. Add timeline + actions to the incident doc. Great work team. :tada:
Carla (sre): ack handoff. I'll own the postmortem and coordinate with Ben, Maya, Dan.
incident-bot: Incident state changed -> MITIGATED. Incident ID: 1789456000. Postmortem assigned: Carla (sre), Ben (infra), Maya (eng-platform), Dan (ml-eng).
